Salted Fish||A building in this settlement produces Salted Fish, a trade resource.
Rendered from the great whales of the northern seas. It lights the lamps of every city that can afford them.
Whale Oil||A building in this settlement produces Whale Oil, a trade resource.
Taken by Druchii corsairs from the sea dragons of the cold seas off Naggaroth. A cloak of it turns a blade.

Sea Dragon Hide||A building in this settlement produces Sea Dragon Hide, a trade resource.
Cane spirit from the hot coasts. Sartosa and the Vampire Coast float on it.
Rum||A building in this settlement produces Rum, a trade resource.
Golden resin washed up on the Sea of Claws shores, prized by jewellers and wizards.
Amber||A building in this settlement produces Amber, a trade resource.
Wheat, rye and barley from working farms. Bread for cities and fodder for armies.
Grain||A building in this settlement produces Grain, a trade resource.
Bretonnian destriers, Kislevite steppe horses, Arabyan coursers, Ellyrian steeds, Averland's herds and the Druchii's Dark Steeds, bred for war.
Warhorses||A building in this settlement produces Warhorses, a trade resource.
Halfling leaf from the Moot, smoked in every tavern from Altdorf to Marienburg.
Pipeweed||A building in this settlement produces Pipeweed, a trade resource.
Printed tomes and copied scrolls from the great presses, colleges and libraries.
Books||A building in this settlement produces Books, a trade resource.
Pressed in the groves of Tilea and Estalia, shipped across the Middle Sea.
Olive Oil||A building in this settlement produces Olive Oil, a trade resource.
Woven in the lowland provinces of Cathay. It is what the Ivory Road carries west.
Silk||A building in this settlement produces Silk, a trade resource.
Leaf from the terraced hills of Cathay, steeped from Wei-Jin to Nan-Gau.
Tea||A building in this settlement produces Tea, a trade resource.
Green stone quarried in Cathay's mountains, carved into charms and statues.
Jade||A building in this settlement produces Jade, a trade resource.
Black fuel dug beside the iron seams. Every forge and furnace burns it.
Coal||A building in this settlement produces Coal, a trade resource.
Veins of silver found in mountain mines already worked for iron, gems or gold, and in the Dwarfs' Underdeep.
Silver||A building in this settlement produces Silver, a trade resource.
Meteoric iron found only deep beneath the old Dwarf holds. Nothing forged is harder.
Gromril||A building in this settlement produces Gromril, a trade resource.
Liquid metal cooked out of cinnabar in volcanic rock. Alchemists and engineers pay well for it.
Quicksilver||A building in this settlement produces Quicksilver, a trade resource.
Yellow sulphur scraped from the vents of the Dark Lands, every obsidian field and the Dwarfs' deepest workings.
Brimstone||A building in this settlement produces Brimstone, a trade resource.
Hashut's own metal, cast in the forges of the Chaos Dwarfs.
Brass||A building in this settlement produces Brass, a trade resource.
Saltpetre from the salt pans, ground with charcoal and sulphur by the races that know the secret.
Blackpowder||A building in this settlement produces Blackpowder, a trade resource.
The light, bright metal of the elves, found only in the rock of Ulthuan.
Ithilmar||A building in this settlement produces Ithilmar, a trade resource.
Bones from the dragon-holds of Caledor and the old dragon graveyards.
Dragon Bone||A building in this settlement produces Dragon Bone, a trade resource.
Brilliant feathers of Lustria's jungle birds and serpents, worth their weight in gold in the courts of the Old World.
Lustrian Plumes||A building in this settlement produces Lustrian Plumes, a trade resource.
A poison flower of the southern jungles, sought by assassins and Witch Elves.
Black Lotus||A building in this settlement produces Black Lotus, a trade resource.
Frankincense and myrrh from the deserts of Araby, burned in temples and tombs.
Incense||A building in this settlement produces Incense, a trade resource.
Hunting grounds, herds and settlement provisioners fill the barrels. Meat keeps; armies march on it.
Salted Meat||A building in this settlement produces Salted Meat, a trade resource.
Knotted by hand in the cities of Araby, in patterns older than the Empire.
Arabyan Carpets||A building in this settlement produces Arabyan Carpets, a trade resource.
Sour rye drink of Kislev, brewed from black bread. Every stanitsa keeps a barrel.
Kvas||A building in this settlement produces Kvas, a trade resource.
Thick grey hides of the Ogre Kingdoms' rhinox herds, tough enough for armour.
Rhinox Hides||A building in this settlement produces Rhinox Hides, a trade resource.
Honey wine of the Norscan halls, drunk from horns before every raid.
Mead||A building in this settlement produces Mead, a trade resource.
Blown glass from the workshops of Tilea, Estalia, Marienburg and Lothern.
Glassware||A building in this settlement produces Glassware, a trade resource.
Fleece from the sheep that graze the Old World's uplands. Spun and woven in every town.
Wool||A building in this settlement produces Wool, a trade resource.
Fine white ware fired in the kilns of Cathay's lowland cities.
Porcelain||A building in this settlement produces Porcelain, a trade resource.
Brought up by divers on the warm coasts, and worn by every noble who can pay.
Pearls||A building in this settlement produces Pearls, a trade resource.
Wood the living trees of Athel Loren shed by their own will. It is given, never cut.
Starwood||A building in this settlement produces Starwood, a trade resource.
Feathers gathered from the mountain eyries of griffons and pegasi.
Griffon and Pegasus Feathers resource production: %n bundle
Griffon and Pegasus Feathers||A building in this settlement produces Griffon and Pegasus Feathers, a trade resource.
Scales of the wyverns that nest in the Badlands and the Mountains of Mourn.
Wyvern Scales||A building in this settlement produces Wyvern Scales, a trade resource.
Hard ship's biscuit, baked dry for long voyages and campaign wagons. It keeps better than fresh bread.
Hardtack||A building in this settlement produces Hardtack, a trade resource.
Cured hides for boots, harness, armour straps and stretcher slings.
Leather||A building in this settlement produces Leather, a trade resource.
Plain woven cloth for tents, work clothes and clean dressings. A necessity rather than a courtly luxury.
Cloth||A building in this settlement produces Cloth, a trade resource.
Hammers, tongs, chisels and saws. Every work gang needs them; every campaign wears them out.
Tools||A building in this settlement produces Tools, a trade resource.

How goods move between settlement stores. These are fixed for the life of a campaign: change them from the main menu before starting a new one. In a multiplayer campaign they are ignored and every value is the default on every machine. The trade route lines and the Vanilla supply lines box can be changed at any time.
Fixed when a campaign starts. Change it from the main menu before starting a new one.
Each turn an army raids a settlement, it carries off this share of every resource the settlement keeps, into its own nearest settlement as far as that has room. 0 turns this off.
Sacking a settlement carries off this share of every resource it keeps, into the sacker's nearest settlement as far as that has room. 0 turns this off.
Razing a settlement carries off this share of every resource it keeps before it burns. 0 turns this off.

Each turn, trade partners receive this share of removable surplus toward their capital import targets. Keep reserves and cargo already on the road are respected. The goods travel the road between the two capitals, a turn for every 40 hexes, and an army at war with the sender can seize them on the way. 0 turns this off.

Each turn, every faction pays each trade partner this share of the value of what that partner's settlements made that turn, at the value trade agreements put on it. The gold goes to the partner. 0 turns this off.

Trade agreements move resources and import duty only while the road between the two capitals takes no more than this many turns and keeps out of lands at war with, or very unfriendly to, either side. The Trade tab lists the partners cut off and why.

How many shipments of yours can be on the road at once. Sending a resource between your settlements takes one to six turns, by the length of its road, and an army at war with you can seize it on the way. Other factions keep one.
Resources per 100 gold of a recruit
How many resources a recruit takes from your stores for each 100 gold it is worth. 0 turns this off.

Each turn, trade that crosses another faction's lands pays that faction this share of the value of the goods it carries. All the tolls on one cargo together are at most 15%. A faction whose Roads edict is Open charges nothing. Neither do your allies and vassals. 0 turns tolls off.
How likely trouble on the road is on the most dangerous land, each turn. Half as dangerous land is half as likely. 0 turns road encounters off.

Armies eat the provisions they carry once a turn. In your own settlements they refill from the stores, never below what a settlement keeps: Auto keeps 5 turns, and Load fills the army to 10. At sea, or with no settlements, Load buys two meals at 10 gold each, once a turn. Armies cannot refill in foreign lands. Missed meals slow an army and its recovery. Caravans and convoys carry none. This is fixed when a campaign starts: changing it later does nothing to a campaign already under way. In multiplayer it is always on.
Allow local workshops to spend stored inputs on extra batches. Passive production is unchanged. Enable individual recipes in a settlement's Stores view.
Allow optional province services paid each turn with named goods. Enable them in the province capital's Stores view.

Factions no player controls raid, sack, trade, eat, recruit and gain bonuses from their stores as a player does. Off: resources move only when a player's faction is one of the two. Other factions' settlements do not eat or gain bonuses, their grain, beer and kvas do not spoil, and their recruits take nothing. Turns run faster on a slow machine.
An army of a faction no player controls never goes hungry while it stands in one of its own settlements that is not under siege. Off: it goes hungry there when the stores run out.

An army of a faction no player controls buys rations with gold when it is away from its own settlements, as any army can at sea: up to two meals at 10 gold each, once a turn. Off: away from home it eats only what it carried.
Armies of factions no player controls eat half the provisions a player's army eats, rounded up. Off: they eat the same.
Each settlement of a faction no player controls makes, every turn, the provisions it eats at Normal rations: 2 for each settlement level. Off: it makes only what its buildings make.

Each turn, grain loses 4% and beer and kvas 2% of what a store holds above a quarter of its space. With the Great Granary, grain is safe up to half. Hardtack, salted meat, salted fish, wine and every other good never spoil. Off: nothing spoils.

Each turn every settlement eats provisions from its stores. Five turns of provisions left make it Well fed; war materials and luxuries filling a quarter of one store's space give Garrison stocked and Comforts. Off: settlements eat nothing and give no bonuses. Spoilage has its own switch.

The Resource Vault can send a resource between your settlements, buy a Festival, Muster or Great Works with your stores, and sell what your stores hold above half their space. Off: the panel only shows.

Now and then a full store offers a choice: a feast, opening the stores to a besieged garrison, a gift to a neighbour or re-arming an army. Accepting spends the resources. Other factions make the same choices on their own. Off: no events.
Stops the game's random dilemmas, the ones that come up on their own, for every faction. Dilemmas that a campaign's story or this mod's store events bring still come. Off: they come as usual.

A province capital can pay from its stores each turn for Materials on hand, Stable stocked and Arms stocked in every settlement you hold in its province, and can send for resources from the province's other settlements. Off: no province supplies.

Every unit you recruit takes resources from your stores by its type and worth (cavalry and monsters take mounts, infantry and war machines take war materials, the finest also take your rare resource). What the stores lack is paid in your race's own currency where it has one, then in gold. Off: recruiting takes nothing.

Every shipment travels with an escort of its owner's soldiers. An army that reaches it must beat the escort to take the cargo, and you are asked before your army attacks one. Off: an army at war takes a shipment without a fight.

Each faction sets three edicts in the Resource Vault: Rations, Workshops and Roads. Each has three choices. A change waits 10 turns before the next. Other factions choose theirs by their situation. Off: there are no edicts.

Trade agreements and partner contracts pay tolls to the factions whose lands their roads cross. An army at war with either side standing within 3 hexes of the road stops that agreement's trade for the turn. Off: no tolls and no blockades.

Bandits, highwaymen and washed-out roads can meet your cargo on the road. Dangerous lands meet them more often. You choose what to do, and some choices lead to a battle. Guards on the Trade tab make it less likely. Off: the roads are safe.

Ticked: the game's own supply lines stay. Each army after your first makes every army cost more upkeep. This mod's roads still carry food to your armies but add no upkeep. Unticked: this mod's supply lines replace them. Races whose armies carry no food keep the game's own rule. So does every race when Army provisions or Army supply lines is off. You can change this during a campaign. In multiplayer it is always unticked.

Each of your armies draws supplies from one of your settlements along a road. The further the road, the more it costs to keep the carts moving. A cut road brings no supplies, and foraging and buying from the locals costs the most. Armies in your own settled land need no road. Land you took in the last few turns feeds no army yet. Turns to settle new land sets how many. With Army provisions off or Vanilla supply lines ticked, the roads add no upkeep.
How far an army can be from one of your settlements and still be supplied, in turns of travel. Past half of that the road is stretched. Further away the road is cut.
Turns before a settlement you take can supply your armies. 0: at once.
